cards.explanation: The answer is 250. The text says these men of Israel were “…renowned as leaders of the congregation and representatives in the assembly.” (Numbers 16:2) These aren't strangers wandering in off the road. These are the folks with name tags that everybody recognizes. That's 250 big names joining one rebellion against Moses.

The answer is that they're all holy and the LORD is in their midst. That's their whole argument. They say, “…everyone in the entire congregation is holy, and the LORD is in their midst.” Then they ask why Moses and Aaron exalt themselves above the assembly of the LORD. It sounds like a point about the whole camp, but the target is Moses and Aaron.

The answer is that he falls facedown, before Moses says one word back. Most of us would be busy loading up a comeback, friends. The text doesn't tell us why he does it, and I'm not going to guess for it. It just says, "When Moses heard this, he fell facedown." (Numbers 16:4) His words to Korah and all his followers come after.

The answer is censers. Moses tells Korah and his followers to take censers and put fire and incense in them in the presence of the LORD. A censer is what you carry that fire and incense in. The next day, the LORD will show whom He chooses.

The answer is True. Korah's crew told Moses and Aaron, “You have taken too much upon yourselves!” Moses answers, “It is you sons of Levi who have taken too much upon yourselves!” He points their charge back at them and names exactly who he means. Clean return.

The answer is the priesthood as well. Moses says it plainly: “He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites, but you are seeking the priesthood as well.” The Levites already got the work at the LORD's tabernacle. Now they want the priesthood on top of it. Moses is asking if what they've been given isn't enough.

The answer is False. Moses says, “Therefore, it is you and all your followers who have conspired against the LORD!” Then he asks about Aaron, “…who is he that you should grumble against him?” Two different words there: conspired against the LORD, grumbled against Aaron.

The answer is a land flowing with milk and honey. You'd never guess it, but that's their word for Egypt. Dathan and Abiram, two Reubenites in Korah's rebellion, say, “…you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness?” Then in the next verse they use that same phrase for the land they haven't reached yet. Milk and honey on both labels, friends.

The answer is that Moses made himself ruler over them. Dathan and Abiram ask, “Must you also appoint yourself as ruler over us?” (Numbers 16:13) Watch that little word “also,” because they've just said Moses brought them up to kill them in the wilderness, and now they pile this on top. It's like someone who hands you a full list of complaints and then says, "Oh, and another thing."

The answer is False. Dathan and Abiram say to Moses, “…you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards.” No admitting here. They're complaining that those things haven't happened.

The answer is donkey. Moses tells the LORD, "I have not taken one donkey from them or mistreated a single one of them." (Numbers 16:15) The text says Moses is very angry when he says it, right after asking the LORD not to regard their offering. He's saying he hasn't taken even one from them. The text doesn't say why he names a donkey, so I'll just leave it right there.

The answer is False. Moses says to Korah, “You and all your followers are to appear before the LORD tomorrow—you and they and Aaron.” Then he adds that Aaron is to present his censer as well. Aaron is in the test right alongside them.

The answer is the glory of the LORD. When Korah has gathered his whole assembly against Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, “…the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole congregation.” It isn't just for the leaders. The whole congregation sees it.

The answer is False. Moses and Aaron don't quietly step away. They fall facedown and say, “O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, when one man sins, will You be angry with the whole congregation?” They speak up for the people.

The answer is man. Moses and Aaron ask, “O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, when one man sins, will You be angry with the whole congregation?” They're lying facedown when they say it. I think that's a brave question to ask from the ground.
The answer is False. Moses goes to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel follow him. He has company the whole way over. They're right there behind him.

The answer is that they'll be swept away. Moses tells the congregation, “Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins.” That's a serious reason to keep your hands to yourself. The people moved away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan and Abiram.

The answer is that the earth opens and swallows them. Moses says, “…if the LORD brings about something unprecedented, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them so that they go down alive into Sheol, then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt.” This is a heavy part of the passage. It's the sign Moses names ahead of time.

The answer is True, and the timing is the point. The text says, “As soon as Moses had finished saying all this, the ground beneath them split open…” Nothing sits between his last word and the ground splitting. It's a heavy moment, friends.
The answer is fled. At their cries, all the people of Israel who were around them fled, saying, “The earth may swallow us too!” That's what they say as they run. This is a heavy moment, friends.

The answer is that fire from the LORD consumes them. The text says, “And fire came forth from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense.” They're the ones who stood there with their censers. It's a heavy ending to the test Moses set up.

The answer is to hammer them into sheets for the altar. The LORD says, “…hammer them into sheets to overlay the altar, for these were presented before the LORD, and so have become holy.” They will serve as a sign to the Israelites. So the censers end up on the altar.

The answer is Aaron. The reminder is “…that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to offer incense before the LORD, lest he become like Korah and his followers.” Korah's line runs back through Izhar, Kohath and Levi, and the reminder points to Aaron's descendants instead. The altar's new covering is there for everyone to see.

The answer is True. The day after the ground swallowed Korah's men and fire took the 250, the people turn on Moses and Aaron with, “You have killed the LORD’s people!” (Numbers 16:41) After all that, the complaining is right back. I think this one is heavy, and it shows how quickly the grumbling can return.

The answer is to go to the congregation and make atonement. Moses tells Aaron, “Take your censer, place fire from the altar in it, and add incense. Go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them…” The censer is for the people out in the middle of the assembly. Aaron has a task to do and not much time.
The answer is that the plague has already begun. Moses says, “…wrath has come out from the LORD; the plague has begun.” So every moment matters. It's why he says to go quickly.
The answer is between the living and the dead. The text says, “He stood between the living and the dead, and the plague was halted.” It's a heavy picture. Aaron stands right at the line.

The answer is False. Aaron runs into the middle of the assembly, offers the incense and makes atonement for the people. Then the text says, “…the plague was halted.” It stops with Aaron standing between the living and the dead.

The answer is fourteen thousand seven hundred. The text says, “But those who died from the plague numbered 14,700, in addition to those who had died on account of Korah.” That's a heavy number. It tells you how serious the plague was.
